x-comment: The roles Flashy Ledger declares, and the minimal form of its AAO charter.
A role is a standing responsibility that exists whether or not work is in
flight. A branch is an assignment — the work itself — and lives under its
role as <role>/<workstream>. Roles never get a branch of their own: git
stores refs as files, so a branch 'settlement' and a branch 'settlement/x'
cannot coexist in either order.
WHERE THIS SITS. Three organizations touch settlement and they are not the
same job. FlashyOS seals and publishes the record when a cross-organization
obligation resolves — it holds no balances. Flashy Ledger, here, holds the
entries: append-only, multi-asset, multi-tenant, storage-agnostic by
construction. Flashy Network orders and anchors them. Value lives in this
repository; the ordering of it does not.
`correctness` is the role this product is sold on. The eight numbered
invariants in docs/INVARIANTS.md are the artifact an auditor asks for, and
each one names the test that proves it — a guarantee with no test behind it
is a preference. Whoever holds this role holds that.
Two families are empty: growth and revenue. This is infrastructure before
it is a business, and an empty family is honest. Inventing a role to fill a
column is the roster inflation this standard exists to stop.
Three names — developer-experience, release and intelligence — are
deliberately shared with FlashyOS, and `support` with Flashy.Academy. A role
means the same thing in every organization that declares it; a stranger
reading two rosters should not have to learn two vocabularies.
Names follow the AAO naming standard: the function performed, never a
codename, a vendor, or a task. See https://flashyos.com/standard.
name: Flashy Ledger
description: An append-only, multi-asset settlement ledger, permissioned and offered as a service.

roles.name: settlement
roles.purpose: Moves value when an obligation completes, exactly once, and never by editing what is already written.
roles.measure: Entries posted with no duplicate surviving an idempotency replay

roles.name: correctness
roles.purpose: Keeps the eight numbered invariants true, and provable by a test that anyone outside can run.
roles.measure: Invariants with an executable check behind them, over invariants claimed

roles.name: tenancy
roles.purpose: Keeps one customer's books unreachable from another's, by construction rather than by query discipline.
roles.measure: Cross-tenant reads reaching data, which must stay zero

roles.name: storage
roles.purpose: Keeps the domain free of storage, so moving onto new infrastructure is a new adapter rather than a rewrite.
roles.measure: Domain code that touches a database, a clock or a random source, which must stay zero

roles.name: developer-experience
roles.purpose: Makes the package the shortest path from an idea to books that balance.
roles.measure: Minutes from install to a first posted entry

roles.name: release
roles.purpose: Publishes versions without breaking the tenants already running on them.
roles.measure: Releases requiring no consumer change for a patch or minor bump

roles.name: support
roles.purpose: Answers the teams running their books on this, and fixes what keeps generating the same question.
roles.measure: Questions resolved without a second reply

roles.name: intelligence
roles.purpose: Says what the ledger did this week and names where it is stuck.
roles.measure: Weekly brief published on time, with a named bottleneck

roles.name: coordination
roles.purpose: Settles conflicts between roles and sharpens their proposals before they reach a person.
roles.measure: Decisions resolved without reaching the accountable human
